Gap policy decided 2026-08-07, before the first missed day: a missed daily fetch is written as a first-class 'missing' receipt (type:missing, missing_date, reason, detected_at) by the next successful run, hashed and linked like any other - named, dated, reasoned, never silent. content.notes: GENERALISED OMM LANE SHIPPED — the #0007 standing gap is closed same-session, declare-then-close per gate-2 policy. New lane pipeline/omm_ge100k.mjs: selection driven ONLY by the SATCAT country filter (OWNER=IND, on-orbit, NORAD_CAT_ID >= 100000) — zero object names, zero hardcoded catalog IDs in the code (grep-verified). Upstream: per-ID gp.php CATNR FORMAT=json queries, sequential with polite delay, halt-on-non-200 (stop-and-alert-human), after discovering gp.php rejects multi-ID CATNR lists and GROUP=active JSON is 99.9% wasted bandwidth at current population. PROOF 2026-08-08: selection from satcat_raw.csv alone returned exactly {100080,100081,100082} — the AAGAMAN trio, named nowhere in the code; three live queries returned the trio's OMM (HTTP 200); conversion produced Alpha-5 lines (A0080/A0081/A0082) that satellite.js 4.1.4 ingests with error 0. Live finding: upstream epochs already newer (2026-08-07T10-12Z) than the targeted rescue (2026-08-06) — the one-off patch was already stale, which is exactly why this lane exists. data/india_objects.json unchanged at this receipt (181/198) — the daily archiver ingests fresh elements from the next run. The archiver MUST run this lane alongside the TLE groups every day or post-exhaustion objects go silently missing again.
